treatment: Salvage prostate-bed RT + 24 months bicalutamide vs salvage prostate-bed RT + placebo
population: 760 eligible men after radical prostatectomy with pT3N0 disease or pT2N0 with positive margins and PSA 0.2–4.0 ng/mL
benefitText: At 18 years, overall survival was 52.9% with salvage RT plus 24 months of bicalutamide versus 43.1% with salvage RT plus placebo, an absolute improvement of 9.8 percentage points (adjusted HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.67–1.00; one-sided P=.025). The 18-year incidence of prostate-cancer death was 18% vs 28% and metastatic prostate cancer was 22% vs 31%. NNT 11 is based on the 18-year overall-survival difference.
harmText: Gynecomastia occurred in 69.7% with bicalutamide versus 10.9% with placebo, an absolute excess of 58.8 percentage points (NNH 2). This is the toxicity endpoint used for NNH. Late radiation-related bladder, bowel and hematologic toxicity was similar between groups; grade 3–4 bladder toxicity was 7.0% vs 6.7% and bowel toxicity 2.7% vs 1.6% in the original report.
clinicalQuestion: In men with biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy receiving salvage prostate-bed radiotherapy, does adding 24 months of antiandrogen therapy improve long-term survival and reduce metastases?
refs: Shipley WU, et al. N Engl J Med. 2017;376:417–428.
NRG/RTOG 9601 long-term follow-up. Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys. 2025.
